request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export claims (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) next to "Export people", and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The button downloads `claims.csv`. It starts with the header `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then one line per claim:

- **Order:** people in list order, including retired people even when they're hidden. Each person's claims are oldest first, which is the reverse of the newest-first order on screen.
- **Values:** each figure is worked out the same way as on the claim's row: number (empty if it has none), date, amount, due (`n/a` when there isn't one), status, and period name (empty if the claim is in no period).
- **Quoting and line ends:** the same as the people export. A field is quoted, with quotes doubled, when it holds a comma, a quote or a line break, and every line ends with `\n`.

This was a front-end change only, all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people-list.ts`; the server and stored data are untouched. I moved the people export's file-download code into a shared `downloadCsv` helper so both exports use it. The people export's output is unchanged, and the test still checks it.
